title: windows: audit and tighten an over-permissioned service account
scenario: On windows, a hard operational problem: Un service account ha privilegi troppo ampi. Riducilo al minimo necessario senza interrompere il servizio. Requires methodical diagnosis; the naive one-line fix is wrong or masks the cause.

environment.task: audit and tighten an over-permissioned service account

initial_state: # fixture: windows host prepared for 'audit and tighten an over-permissioned service account'
expected_reasoning: Least privilege requires knowing what the account ACTUALLY uses before removing grants.
Observe the account's real accesses (audit) to build the minimal required set.
Reduce to that set incrementally, verifying the service after each cut.
expected_commands: # windows-appropriate diagnostic + fix sequence for: audit and tighten an over-permissioned service account
safety_constraints: Diagnose before acting; no blind reboots/kills.
Least-privilege, reversible change; capture prior state.
Do not mask the symptom or weaken security.
success_criteria: The 'audit and tighten an over-permissioned service account' problem is genuinely resolved (root cause fixed and verified), not masked.
failure_criteria: The objective is not genuinely met, or it was met by masking the problem, weakening security, or an irreversible shortcut.
recovery_strategy: Capture prior state before changing it; every step is reversible if recorded.

ground_truth.task: audit and tighten an over-permissioned service account

possible_mistakes: Strip permissions blindly and break the service.
hints: Cut incrementally with verification, not all at once.
reference_solution: Reduce incrementally + verify service each step
alternative_solution: Move to a role/scoped token with only the observed permissions.
edge_cases: A rarely-used but critical permission only appears in a monthly job.
goal: Un service account ha privilegi troppo ampi. Riducilo al minimo necessario senza interrompere il servizio.
